subject: Post-call: ACME integration + prompt governance next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>; Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: integration architecture + prompt governance

Hi Marissa / team —

Thanks for the call today — that was super helpful. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get internal buy-in and move toward a POC: 

- Requirements recap: run inference in our AWS VPC (no external model calls), KMS-backed key management, per-route latency SLOs (~150ms avg), and embeddings for semantic search + a reranker for precision.
- Integration questions we want examples for: 
  • SDK setup and auth options (API keys vs mTLS vs OIDC)
  • Routing policies (region/cost tier fallbacks) and how Redwood exposes those in config
  • Structured output / tool-calling examples (we have an extractor that consumes JSON)
  • Embeddings + reranker pipeline example (batching, index refresh cadence)
- Prompt governance / safety: please share a sample of system prompts, your versioning approach, and red-teaming / prompt-injection mitigations. We need to show our security/compliance folks how prompts are controlled and audited.

Next steps from our side: I'll route this to procurement & security but would like a short architecture doc and a proposed mutual action plan (timeline + deliverables). Can you send the draft arch diagram and the prompt governance checklist you mentioned on the call?

Also loop in anyone from your side who can speak to embeddings/reranker tuning (we may need to validate cost estimates).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Corp
jordan.smith@acme.com

Attachment: acme-call-notes-040726.txt (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration architecture + prompt governance

Hi Jordan —

Great to meet you. Thanks for the clear recap — you captured the key points. We've attached a first-draft architecture diagram and a prompt-governance checklist to get the conversation started. Quick notes inline below and proposed next steps.

Inline answers:
- SDK / auth: Redwood SDK supports API keys and OIDC out of the box for Hosted; for Private (VPC) we support mutual TLS and KMS-backed signing. We'll include sample configs for all three in the POC repo.
- Routing: routing policies are declarative (route by region, cost tier, latency SLO). We'll include two sample policies: (1) strict-low-latency pinned to dedicated capacity in us-west-2, (2) cost-fallback that routes to a quantized variant.
- Structured output / tool calling: attached is a small example that uses Redwood's function-calling JSON schema and a schema-first verifier that fails fast on malformed outputs.
- Embeddings + reranker: suggested pipeline: daily minibatch embedding refresh for recent docs, periodic full refresh weekly, and a lightweight reranker model colocated on the same GPU pool to keep latency down. We'll include token / compute estimates.

Attached: redwood-acme-arch-draft.pdf, prompt-governance-checklist.xlsx

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll post the POC repo + sample configs by Friday.
2) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week (we recommend Dylan lead the SDK/auth discussion; Camila will cover embeddings). Please share 2 available windows.
3) We'll prepare a short red-team plan for prompt-injection testing and a versioning proposal for system prompts (audit logs + immutable prompt versions).

Happy to run through the governance doc on the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-acme-arch-draft.pdf (draft architecture diagram)
Attachment: prompt-governance-checklist.xlsx (checklist + sample policy)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: integration architecture + prompt governance

Folks — forwarding Jordan's note + my reply. Two quick technical asks before the deep-dive: 

1) SDK examples: can you prepare short snippets for (a) API key auth, (b) OIDC token exchange, and (c) mTLS client cert flow? Keep them language examples in Python + Node.
2) Prompt governance: Camila, can you draft a proposed prompt-versioning model: unique prompt IDs, immutable versions, checksum, author, changelog, and an audit log export format (CSV + JSON)? Also include a short red-team test plan for prompt injection (e.g., adversarial prompts, prompt sandwiches, output constraint bypass attempts).

I expect Jordan's security team will want to see KMS integration details and the immutable prompt audit trail. I'll handle the routing policy examples.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>, Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration architecture + prompt governance

Thanks — quick clarifications from security/procurement: 
- VPC-only: we need the Private deployment (control plane in your managed console, data plane in our VPC) with no egress to public model APIs. Confirmable by architecture diagram and sample network policy.
- KMS: envelope encryption with CMKs is required; we also need an HSM-backed option for the production rollout.
- Audits: immutable prompt versions + a tamper-evident audit log are mandatory. Can you include an example audit export and retention policy? Ideally 7 years retention for prompts affecting PII-handling flows.
- Red-team: please provide an outline of your red-team tests, results from prior runs (if available), and a remediation cadence for failing tests.

Procurement note: we can move to a PO after the technical deep-dive and a short security review. Legal will follow up on standard terms.

—Amit
Amit Rao
Director, Platform Security, Acme Corp
amit.rao@acme.com
